# Pinned to non-heir-backoff=1.5 (the v1 default): this file tests v1's
# "non-heirs back off so the heir fires first" ordering. Since
# DESIGN_UPDATE.md D3 the default is 1.0 (stock timers), which only keeps
# the heir first once D1's short heir timeout lands.

# T4.8 (TASKS.md) -- "all HeirRaft flags ON" interaction smoke test. Turning
# every flag on for every pre-existing golden file isn't feasible (see
# heir_conformance_test.go and RESEARCH_LOG.md 2026-07-21 for why: exact
# byte-for-byte output comparison would mass-mismatch for reasons that
# aren't bugs). Instead, this one file deliberately turns HeirElection,
# HeirLogPriority and GracefulHandover on together and chains T4.4-T4.7's
# mechanisms through a single realistic scenario, to shake out any
# cross-flag interaction that no single task's own test would exercise:
# selection + heir-first dispatch -> proactive handover -> the *new* leader
# re-selecting its own heir -> that new heir crash-timing out first when the
# new leader dies too.

log-level error
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4) index=2 heir-election=true heir-log-priority=true graceful-handover=true degrade-window=2 mutable-stability-score=200 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4) index=2 heir-election=true heir-log-priority=true graceful-handover=true stability-score=255 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4) index=2 heir-election=true heir-log-priority=true graceful-handover=true stability-score=150 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

add-nodes 1 voters=(1,2,3,4) index=2 heir-election=true heir-log-priority=true graceful-handover=true stability-score=100 non-heir-backoff=1.5
----
ok

# Crash path, chained on top of a handover-selected heir: leader 2 is now
